item.title: Police arrest escaped prisoner in Alice Springs
item.description: UPDATED: NT Police have located 20-year-old Murphy Ward who escaped from Corrections while in the custody of private firm G4S on Monday afternoon, but police had failed to inform the public that Ward was recently charged with a series of violent crimes, including aggravated assault and choking, strangling and suffocating.

item.title: Police call for witnesses, dashcam footage of last Friday’s Pinelands fatal pedestrian strike
item.description: Detectives investigating the death of a man who was struck by a vehicle on the inbound lane of the Stuart Highway at Pinelands on Friday, February 27, have appealed to the public for witnesses or dashcam footage of the incident.

item.title: AirAsia cancels two Darwin flight services
item.description: AirAsia will discontinue its Darwin to Bali and Kuala Lumpur routes less than a year after launching due to operating below a 70 per cent load factor, making them economically unsustainable, the company has indicated, while the NT Government has pledged to review its taxpayer-funded air subsidy scheme in the wake of the cancelled routes.

item.title: Palmerston man arrested with child abuse material
item.description: A 25-year-old Palmerston man has been arrested and charged after a raid of his home yesterday uncovered child abuse and animal sexual abuse material, NT Police said.

item.title: NT Criminal Court list – with charges – Mar 06
item.description: The 152 names facing criminal courts in the Northern Territory for Friday, March 06, 2026. This list includes all the charges.

item.title: Federal inquiry ordered into racism, hate and violence against First Nations people
item.description: A federal parliamentary inquiry into "racism, hate and violence directed at First Nations people" has been struck amid a "reported increase" of online racism directed at Indigenous Australians that will report back by September, NT Senator and Federal Minister for Indigenous Australians Malarndirri McCarthy has announced.

item.title: ‘Diverse and modern’: NT Cattlemen’s Association attempts to distance itself from Connolly’s remarks
item.description: The NT Cattlemen's Association has been forced to publicly acknowledge it works with Indigenous people and employs women in leadership roles as part of a "diverse and modern" NT cattle industry, following comments from NT Administrator and former NTCA president David Connolly, who claimed on Monday that his racist, sexist and homophobic social media posts, that also included joking about domestic violence and date rape, were a reflection of "the pastoral world".

item.title: ‘Confronting scene’: Fraud investigation leads to grisly discovery of dead dogs at Tennant Creek property
item.description: Several malnourished and dead dogs were discovered by police at a Tennant Creek property on Wednesday while attending on another matter that has led to animal cruelty charges against a 57-year-old man in a scene police described as "confronting" for officers, with the number of dead dogs on the property "incredibly concerning".

item.title: More CDU course failures emerge as another program under review over accreditation concerns
item.description: EXCLUSIVE: Another Charles Darwin University program has been called into question amid the recently disclosed TAFE accreditation failure, with the Bachelor of Humanitarian Aid and Development course the subject of an external review following multiple student complaints into delayed fieldwork placements, over-enrolled classes and serious staffing issues, including allegations responsible instructors were not properly qualified.

item.title: Another Labor govt investment goes under with taxpayers on the hook – but no inquiry needed, Chief Minister says
item.description: A rocket launching company the previous Labor government invested more than $5 million of public funds into has gone into liquidation, with the Chief Minister mocking Labor again for their poor investment decisions, but refusing to answer questions about whether she would now call a public inquiry into how Labor wasted millions of taxpayer money investing in doomed private business enterprises.
